claims.text: The proposed material is a single-phase high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
The proposed alloy is outside the well-studied Nb-Ta and titanium-rich alloy families.
A minor elemental substitution can enhance local chemical short-range order without causing phase separation.
The substitution can preserve large-scale disorder and the single-phase solid-solution state.
The controlled substitution produces atomic-scale variations in local bonding environments.
Increasing local chemical short-range order increases electron-phonon coupling strength.
Modified local atomic environments create regions of enhanced electron-phonon coupling.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling facilitates stronger Cooper pairing.
Stronger Cooper pairing raises the superconducting transition temperature relative to a maximally random baseline.
An alloy variant with increased local order will exhibit a measurable increase in Tc relative to the disordered baseline.
Increasing local order will produce corresponding changes in the phonon density of states.
Changes in phonon density of states are indicative of altered electron-phonon interactions.
Chemical or structural disorder can affect superconducting behavior.
A critical amount of disorder can suppress superconductivity near an Anderson quantum phase transition.
Strongly disordered metals may exhibit Tc enhancement when tuned to a quantum critical point within a BCS framework.
The predicted behavior applies only while the single-phase state is maintained without phase segregation.
The proposed effect is relevant in the low-temperature regime where superconductivity is observed.
Atom probe tomography or high-resolution transmission electron microscopy can characterize the proposed local chemical order.
The hypothesis is falsified if induced local order yields neither a statistically significant Tc increase nor a detectable electron-phonon-coupling modification relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies an elemental substitution, which ordinarily changes overall elemental composition, while also claiming that overall composition is maintained; the experiment further requires the substituted and control samples to have identical overall composition. No composition-preserving substitution scheme is explained.
